# Seattle's Floating Landmark

## The Center for Wooden Boats floating campus is a Landmark as designated by the City of Seattle. This includes the floating structures of our South Lake Union home (also known as Waterway 4) and The Old Boathouse (also known as the Wagner Floating Home).

Thank you to every community member who wrote letters to the Landmarks Preservation Board or testified at hearings, to researcher [Sarah Martin](https://sarahjacksonmartin.com/), and to [4Culture](https://www.4culture.org/), which supported the application. [Donate](https://www.cwb.org/give)

(Embedded video)

### By designating our floating structures as historical landmarks, we will be able to secure the preservation of our history and continue to share the space for one and all.

The floating campus grew out of a plan championed by co-founders Dick and Colleen Wagner. Public historian [Sarah Martin](https://sarahjacksonmartin.com/) presented her research for the landmark applications. Sponsors included CWB, the Wagner family, 4Culture and [Historic Seattle](https://historicseattle.org/).

[View the CWB Historical Landmark Application](https://www.cwb.org/s/LandmarkCompleteApplication_02-17-2021_FINAL.pdf)

[View the presentation PDF](https://www.cwb.org/s/ThirdFriday_03-19-2021_Final.pdf)

### What is a Historical Landmark?
To be designated, a property must meet at least one of the City of Seattle's six [landmark designation criteria](http://www.seattle.gov/neighborhoods/programs-and-services/historic-preservation/landmarks#nominationanddesignationprocess):
- A. Historic events
- B. Association with significant people
- C. Cultural, political or economic heritage
- D. Architectural style, period or method of construction
- E. Work of a notable designer or builder
- F. Visual prominence in the neighborhood or city

The nomination report addresses both the associative and physical significance of the campus.
